message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck (standard Uno deck).
• Each player draws 7 cards.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Turn the top card of the draw pile face‑up to start the discard pile. If it’s an action card, follow its effect immediately. | | **Turn Order** | Clockwise (unless a “Reverse” card is played). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches either the **color** or the **number/symbol** of the top discard.
• If you can’t play, you must draw one card from the draw pile.
• If that drawn card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color and the next player draws four cards. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise you risk a challenge.) | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you play your **second‑to‑last** card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player calls it out, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The first player to discard all of their cards wins the round. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of the cards left in each opponent’s hand:
• Number cards = face value.
• Draw Two, Reverse, Skip = 20 points each.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points each.
Winner of the round receives that total. | | **Game End** | First player to reach the target score (usually 500) wins the game. | **House‑Rule Variations (optional)** - **Stacking**: Allow players to stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards instead of drawing. - **No Wild Draw Four Challenge**: Simplify by removing the challenge rule. - **Different Starting Hand Size**: 5 or 9 cards instead of 7. - **Custom Decks**: Use themed decks or add extra action cards. Enjoy a fast‑paced, colorful card game that’s easy to learn but hard to master!
